extracted.intended_audience: scientists and educated general readers (physicians, members of scientific societies)
extracted.subtask_description: Magazine miscellany containing book reviews, meeting reports, notes, and short expositions on scientific and practical topics; includes implicit evaluative criteria for books, reports, and practices described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook clarity and logical arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: It presents the principles of the science plainly, clearly, and briefly, in well-framed sentences, and is arranged after a logical classification of the divisions and subdivisions of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textbooks should present principles plainly, clearly, and briefly; use well-framed sentences; follow a logical classification of divisions and subdivisions. Practical sections (e.g., hygiene) should be explicitly useful. Illustrations may be provided as separate plates. The work is designed to be supplemented by study of other, more complete works (a partial list may be given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility vs. depth (intended audience)
rubrics_metrics.description: This volume has been made for physicians, but it would be a mistake to infer that it had been exclusively prepared for them, and will not be of great value to non-professional readers. The information it contains ought to be widely diffused, and persons of ordinary intelligence can learn a great deal from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a work balances professional depth with accessibility: is the material diffusible to non-specialists? Does it reward careful attention though it may not be mastered without study?

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of quackish or misleading content
rubrics_metrics.description: There are, moreover, abundance of quackish books on these subjects which so mislead people that they are worse than nothing. It is, therefore, important that the circulation of really valuable volumes on such topics ... should be in every way promoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess factual reliability and whether the work corrects or perpetuates misleading 'quackish' claims. Preference for works that do not mislead and that contribute genuinely useful, evidence-based information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of didacticism and narrative in novels
rubrics_metrics.description: It was of too didactic a quality to suit the tastes of novel-readers in search of mere sensation. It is full of moralizings, and, although the topics are secular enough, it is rather preachy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fiction, consider whether excessive didacticism or moralizing undermines popular appeal; weigh instructive or philosophical side-discussions against the demands of plot and reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative impartiality and practical remediation (public-health/engineering reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: This work is the result of investigations made by an impartial inquirer ... An amazing prevalence of defects ... Illustrations are given of bad drainage ... The dangers which bad sewers and drains entail are forcibly presented; and suggestions are given for remedying and preventing the evils which they occasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess investigational work for impartiality, thorough description of defects, use of concrete case illustrations, tracing of sickness to causes, and provision of practical, actionable remedies and preventive suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical completeness for a how-to or guide book
rubrics_metrics.description: He has therefore put all the information that was sought in the questions in this little volume. The book describes the 'Wilderness' country and the conditions of the camp; considers the practicability of weak persons wintering in the region described, furnishes a summary of several cases that have been treated in the method recommended, or one like it, and considers the questions of necessary outfit and expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides should comprehensively answer common inquiries, describe locale and conditions, assess practicability especially for vulnerable readers, summarize relevant case histories, and give concrete information on required equipment and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management rules for men working in compressed air
rubrics_metrics.description: Professor Woodward ... establishes a system of rules for the management of men at work in compressed air, embodying the principles that only sound men should be employed, that they should be guarded against exhaustion, that they should not be exposed with unnecessary suddenness to the change from a compressed to the normal atmosphere; and that such a supply of heat should be given every man that he could lose a large amount and still have plenty left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical workplace safety rules derived from observation: employ only medically sound workers; prevent physical exhaustion; avoid sudden decompression; ensure adequate thermal protection. Recommendations should be grounded in observed symptoms, case counts, and post-mortem findings where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use careful empirical observation to infer causation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is also worthy of remark that none of the men were ever attacked on entering the caisson, and none were ever sick while in the air-chamber, no matter how long the watch, but the attack always came on within half an hour after leaving the air-lock, or at the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inferring causes from observational data, pay attention to timing and context of symptoms (e.g., onset after leaving exposure). Such temporal patterns are important evidence when evaluating competing causal theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of anthropological sciences (three divisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Topinard classifies the anthropological sciences in three divisions. The first division, anthropology proper, is general... and special... To the second division he gives the name of ethnography... The third division includes the complementary sciences, among which archaeology, especially prehistoric archaeology, holds the first rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a structured classification when organizing anthropological inquiry: general and special anthropology, ethnography (special and general), and complementary sciences (archaeology, etc.). This taxonomy guides scope, methods, and sources to consult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation of complementary sciences in anthropology
rubrics_metrics.description: A fourth division might be added, consisting of sciences to be consulted. Among them might be included geography, as showing the distribution of peoples, and the topographical conditions of their surroundings; comparative law, as illustrating their social and legislative organizations; architecture and music... sculpture, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anthropological conclusions should be informed by complementary disciplines (geography, comparative law, architecture, music, sculpture, etc.) to illuminate distribution, social organization, and cultural traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of human characteristics into five orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Human characteristics may be arranged, according to their bearing on anthropology and ethnography, in five orders: External physical traits; internal physical traits; physiological traits; pathological traits; and ethnic traits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing populations, categorize observable and relevant human characteristics into external physical, internal physical, physiological, pathological, and ethnic traits; use ethnic traits to encompass customs, institutions, and cultural markers (e.g., burial customs, marriage forms, artificial deformations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution in using linguistic evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Linguistics, which should not be confounded with philology, helps to fill the gaps left by history and archaeology, by indicating the passage of a people through a particular region. Deductions should be made from it with careful consideration, for they are worth no more than those which may be drawn from a custom, a mythological form, or a funeral rite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat linguistic parallels as suggestive but not definitive proof of population movements or racial relationships; weigh linguistic evidence alongside customs, myths, archaeological and other data; avoid over-interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for degree conferral (Ph.D.)
rubrics_metrics.description: A resolution was adopted disapproving the conferring of the degree of Ph. D. except after examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional and professional standards may require formal examination as a prerequisite to conferring advanced degrees; this is presented as a quality/legitimacy standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators of a successful scientific meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: The thirtieth meeting ... was one of the largest and every way most successful ... There was an unusually strong influx of new members, and the regular working force of the Association was well represented. The papers were many and varied, and some of them results of able investigation, and showing a well-sustained activity of original research. Every arrangement for the comfort and the pleasure of the scientists was perfect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure meeting success by breadth and quality of participation (new members, representative working force), number and variety of papers, presence of able/original investigations, and adequacy of arrangements for participants' comfort and social interaction.
